question: Why is multer.memoryStorage() dangerous for uploading large files?

options.text: Memory storage is slower than disk storage
options.explanation: Actually, memory storage is faster (RAM is faster than disk). The problem is not speed but memory consumption. For 100 users uploading 100 MB each = 10 GB RAM

options.text: Files are lost on server restart
options.explanation: This is true, but not the reason it's dangerous. Files in memory storage are always processed immediately (saved to disk/S3). The problem is RAM consumption during upload

options.text: The entire file is stored in RAM as a Buffer -- uploading a 500 MB video will cause OOM (Out of Memory)
Memory storage doesn't support multiple files
options.explanation: Memory storage supports single, array, and fields. The problem is that each file is fully loaded into RAM. For small files (<5 MB) this is fine

question: Why shouldn't you trust file.originalname when saving a file?

options.text: The original name can contain path traversal (../../etc/passwd) and overwrite system files
Cyrillic characters in filenames can cause encoding errors
options.explanation: Encoding is a minor issue. The main concern is security. Always generate UUIDs for filenames and save the original name in database metadata

options.text: The filename might be too long for the file system
options.explanation: Length is a secondary concern. The main threat is path traversal. A name like '../../etc/passwd' allows writing a file outside the uploads/ directory

options.text: Two users can upload a file with the same name
options.explanation: Name collision is a problem, but not the main one. Path traversal allows an attacker to overwrite any file on the server, including configuration files

question: Why is checking magic bytes better than checking file extensions?

options.text: File extensions are not supported in Linux
options.explanation: Linux does support extensions, though it doesn't use them for type detection. The problem is that an extension is just part of a filename that a user can change

options.text: Magic bytes check files faster than extension checking
options.explanation: Extension checking is faster (just a string comparison). Magic bytes require reading the first bytes of a file. The advantage is reliability, not speed

options.text: Magic bytes are a signature at the start of a file that cannot be faked by simple renaming (.exe -> .jpg)
Magic bytes only work for images
options.explanation: Magic bytes exist for most formats: PDF (%PDF), ZIP (PK), JPEG (FF D8 FF), PNG (89 50 4E 47). The file-type library recognizes hundreds of formats

question: How does busboy save RAM compared to Multer when uploading files?

options.text: Busboy compresses the file before saving
options.explanation: Busboy doesn't compress files. It parses the multipart stream and passes chunks through the Node.js Stream API. RAM savings come from not fully buffering the file

options.text: Busboy processes the file in streams (chunks of ~64 KB), without loading the entire file into memory
Busboy uses a swap file instead of RAM
options.explanation: Busboy doesn't use swap. It pipes data from the request stream to a write stream. Only the current chunk (~64 KB) is in memory

options.text: Busboy is faster than Multer, so the file passes through RAM faster
options.explanation: Speed doesn't affect RAM consumption. Multer memoryStorage keeps the entire Buffer until processing. Busboy passes chunks as they arrive -- only the current chunk is in RAM
